flat.radio.polar-plots-show-the: Polar plots show the normalised radiation pattern. Azimuth: a dipole's E-plane is a figure eight (maximum radiation broadside to the element) and the H-plane is omnidirectional; a 3-element Yagi has a forward main lobe with the rear lobe strongly suppressed, while square / triangular loops are roughly omnidirectional horizontally (very little directivity). Elevation: a vertical antenna favours low angles (good for DX) and a horizontal loop favours high angles (good for NVIS short-range work). Choosing Dipole (adjustable height) lets you drag the height slider and watch the main lobe change — low heights point up, higher heights lower the take-off angle.

flat.tools.a-series-capacitor-or: A series capacitor or inductor changes only the reactance (sliding along a constant-resistance circle), while a shunt element changes only the susceptance (sliding along a constant-conductance circle). Since the two move in different directions, two elements are enough to push any impedance to the centre. Negative series reactance means a series capacitor; negative shunt susceptance means a shunt inductor.

flat.tools.all-three-prototypes-butterworth: All three prototypes (Butterworth / Chebyshev I / Chebyshev II) are evaluated analytically from their pole and zero positions rather than fitted from tables, so the magnitude, phase and group-delay curves all come from exactly the same transfer function. At the same order, Chebyshev rolls off faster and pays for it with equiripple in the passband or stopband and a more non-linear phase — the trade-off between selectivity and waveform fidelity.

flat.tools.at-100-modulation-m: At 100% modulation (m = 1) the total power is 1.5× and the sidebands carry only one third of it — the carrier holds no information yet eats two thirds of the power. A real antenna impedance varies with frequency, so the figure here is optimistic — best used to compare which matching solution is wider.
flat.tools.the-chart-is-normalised: The chart is normalised to 50Ω: the centre is a perfect match, the upper half is inductive (+jX) and the lower half capacitive (−jX). The dot is the load impedance and can be dragged directly; the blue polyline is the path along which the matching elements push the impedance toward the centre — series elements travel along constant-resistance circles, shunt elements along constant-conductance circles.
flat.tools.the-current-component-set: The current component set does not reach SWR ≤ 2.0 at the centre frequency, so there is no bandwidth to speak of.
flat.tools.the-horizontal-axis-is: The horizontal axis is measured in modulation periods (one period = one full cycle of the modulating signal) and the vertical axis is normalised amplitude; the spectrum's horizontal axis is in units of fm away from the carrier.
